newsitem.title: PERU: Captive Bolivian ambassador cheered by folk music.
newsitem.headline: Captive Bolivian ambassador cheered by folk music.

text.p: The daughter of Bolivian ambassador Jorge Gumucio, who is being held hostage by Marxist guerrillas, brought a smile to her father's face on Friday by playing him some music from home.
Maria Elena Gumucio persuaded police outside the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima to play a cassette of Bolivian folk music over loud speakers, witnesses said.
Gumucio, among 74 hostages held for 24 days by Marxist rebels from the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), appeared at a window of the residence waving and smiling.
"Fine, fine," he mouthed in reply to shouts of "How are you?" from photographers on a nearby roof.

Gumucio and Japanese ambassador Morihisa Aoki, the host of a diplomatic reception stormed by the guerrillas on Dec. 17, are the only ambassadors left inside the residence out of more than a dozen initially captured.
The rebels are using Gumucio as a lever to obtain the release of four MRTA comrades jailed in Bolivia, but that country's government has flatly ruled out any such bargain.
